scenarios.title: Flooding
scenarios.intro: Rivers rise, streets and cellars fill with water.

questions.text: Heavy rain has flooded your street. Your bike is in the underground car park of your building. What do you do?

options.text: Run down quickly and move the bike to a higher place.
Stay out of the car park and leave the bike where it is.
Wait in the car park until the rain stops.

questions.explanation: When there is a risk of flooding, do not go into basements or underground car parks. Do not put yourself in danger to save things. Leave the endangered area right away.
questions.summary: Stay out of basements and underground car parks when it floods, even to save your things.

questions.text: The river near your student flat is very high and fast. You want to walk to the station. Which route do you take?

options.text: The riverside path, because it is the shortest way.
A route away from the river, even if it takes longer.
Over the footbridge, so you can see how high the water is.

questions.explanation: Keep away from rivers and lakes that carry flood water. Surging water can catch you by surprise, and it can wash away the banks and make them collapse.
questions.summary: Keep away from rivers and lakes that carry flood water: the banks can collapse.

questions.text: The flood is over and the water has left your flat. When can you switch the power back on?

options.text: Right away, so you can dry the room with a heater.
As soon as the floor looks dry.
Only after an expert has checked the wiring and appliances.

questions.explanation: Do not switch electricity or gas back on until an expert has checked the lines and appliances. Flush the drinking-water pipes well and, if in doubt, boil the water before you use it.
questions.summary: After a flood, switch power and gas back on only after an expert has checked them.

scenarios.title: Heatwaves
scenarios.intro: Many hot days and warm nights in a row.

questions.text: A heatwave warning is out for your region. You planned a run with friends at 2 p.m. What is the best plan?

options.text: Run at 2 p.m. as planned and bring a sports drink.
Move the run to the early morning or the evening, or skip it.
Run at 2 p.m., but take a shorter route.

questions.explanation: During a heatwave, keep outdoor activities to the morning and evening, and avoid hard physical activity. Stay in the shade and protect yourself from direct sun.
questions.summary: In a heatwave, do sport in the early morning or the evening, not in the heat of the day.

questions.text: How much should you drink on a hot day during a heatwave?

options.text: Regularly through the day, at least 1.5 litres.
Only when you feel thirsty.
Mainly cold beer or iced soft drinks.

questions.explanation: Drink regularly and enough, at least 1.5 litres a day. Do not drink alcohol. Eat fresh, cool and light meals.
questions.summary: Drink regularly, at least 1.5 litres a day, and drink no alcohol.

questions.text: Your room gets very hot during the day. When should you let fresh air in?

options.text: At midday, when the sun is strongest.
Never. Keep the windows shut day and night.
At night and early in the morning, when it is cooler outside.

questions.explanation: Use the cooler night air. Let plenty of outside air through your home at night and early in the morning, before the hot part of the day.
questions.summary: Let fresh air in at night and early in the morning, when it is cooler outside.

scenarios.title: Severe thunderstorms
scenarios.intro: Lightning, hail and strong gusts can arrive within minutes.

questions.text: You see lightning and count 9 seconds until you hear the thunder. About how far away is the storm?

options.text: About 3 km
About 9 km
About 30 km

questions.explanation: Count the seconds between the lightning and the thunder and divide by three. That gives the distance in kilometres: 9 ÷ 3 = about 3 km. The storm is close, so seek shelter in a building or a car.
questions.summary: Seconds between lightning and thunder divided by three = distance in kilometres.

questions.text: You are swimming in a lake with friends when a thunderstorm moves in. What do you do?

options.text: Stay in the water until the rain is over.
Swim out to the raft and wait there.
Get out of the water and go into a building or a car.

questions.explanation: Stay away from water during a thunderstorm. Get out and seek shelter in a building or a car.
questions.summary: When a thunderstorm comes, get out of the water and into a building or a car.

questions.text: You are hiking in open terrain. There is no building or car nearby, and lightning is close. What do you do?

options.text: Lie flat on the ground.
Crouch down low.
Walk down into the dry riverbed to get lower.

questions.explanation: In open terrain, if lightning is nearby, take a crouched position with your feet together, and do not lie flat. Avoid riverbeds, steep slopes and flooded roads.
questions.summary: Caught in the open: crouch down with your feet together, and never lie flat.
